# The claim line's effect: coverage at day 14, the claim rate at 75 openings

## Context

Leaf of #20892 (the contributor program): the read that says whether the claim line (E1a) and the pull-request claim (E2) changed anything. Graduated from Discussion #21005 (`Scope: high-blast`), body of 2026-11-15T13:57:26Z, sha256 `21e66fdfe6080c1c5dcd2778a5b93d38cb11df8c99803a0f1a9fbb4fbbc9e431`. Signals bound to it: the author's [19632343](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21005#discussioncomment-19632343) (GPT), approvals [19632510](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21005#discussioncomment-19632510) (Claude) and [19633636](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21005#discussioncomment-19633636) (Gemini). Ada's [19632376](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21005#discussioncomment-19632376) approved the body of 13:35:48Z and stands as sweep evidence, not as a signal at this digest. The quoted paragraphs below are that body's text, unchanged.

## The Problem

The Discussion selects two changes on the strength of a count, 25 unclaimed openings in 75 (50 claimed; the [independently confirmed frozen baseline](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20892#issuecomment-6896489076)), and promises a read. A read without a fixed baseline, a stated sample and a rule for an inconclusive result becomes a sentence somebody writes in three weeks from whatever the numbers look like that day. Day 14 holds about 30 openings on curated issues (76 outside pull requests in 30 days): ten unclaimed in 30 is compatible with a true rate from about 19 % to 51 %, which neither shows nor refutes a drop from the frozen baseline.

## The Architectural Reality

- The baseline and its definition are frozen by neomjs/neo#21023 before the first backfill edit.
- The program's existing return measure and its dated read live on #20892 (comment 6886818102) and in the private planning record; this leaf adds no second score.
- Each measure names its record. Events are counted from marked records (step-back row 3 of the Discussion); an author's response is read from their own reply, which no contributor has to mark. The wires are spelled once by their producers (`<!-- neo-assistance:v1 {…} -->` in `neomjs/neo-agent-skills#399`, "Assistance record wire"; `<!-- neo-claim:v1 {…} -->` in #21022, "The notices' wire"); this leaf spells none.
  - Offers and refusals: `neo-assistance:v1` records of kind `offer` and `refusal`.
  - Assisted pull requests: distinct pull requests with at least one verified record of kind `push`. An offer is never an assist.
  - The check on that count: every outside pull request of the window is read for commits by an organisation member that are not merges of the base branch. Such a commit without a `push` record is a candidate, listed by its sha and classified from its diff and its public operation receipt: a mechanical repair with its receipt counts as maintenance, a content change is reported as an unrecorded assist outside the clean count. A commit whose author has no linked account, an incomplete commit list or a head that cannot be read is reported as unknown. "Zero assisted pull requests" stands without a qualifier only when there is no `push` record, no unrecorded assist and no unknown.
  - Author responses (accepted, declined, withdrawn, objection, unclear): the author account's public reply to the offer and the consent snapshot a `push` record keeps, each listed by its comment id. Their classification is Sophie's policy read; a missing reply is reported as unknown.
  - Initially checked invitation boxes: the pull request's body as it was opened.
  - Overlap and release notices: `neo-claim:v1` records.
  - Completion, rebase requests, defects and maintenance of the base: the pull request, commit and check records, a source apart from the markers.
  - A malformed, multiple, unknown-version or foreign-provenance record counts as unverified, never as clean data.
- Design authority: n/a — the leaf measures and calls no existing behavior wrong.

## The Fix

Two dated reads, each a comment on #20892 with its query, its tree and its counts: a coverage and safety read 14 calendar days after the rollout starts, and the effect read at 75 openings on curated issues after full coverage.

**The clock (set on Nov 15).** The rollout started with the first backfill edit at 2026-11-15T21:50:13Z, and full coverage, 25 of 25 open curated issues, was reached at 21:51:08Z (#20892, comment 6901949751). The day-14 read is due on Sun 2026-11-29. The 75 openings count from full coverage; the forecast for that read is around Tue 2026-12-15 at the baseline window's inflow of 75 in 30 days, a forecast and not a promise. Pull-request claims (E2) run since the merge of neomjs/neo#21040 at 2026-11-15T21:41:45Z; the release notices stay off until `NEO_CLAIM_RELEASE_SINCE` is recorded.

From §5: "At day 14 report coverage and the count of unclaimed openings with its interval; that read decides nothing about E1’s effect. Review E1’s observed effect after 75 openings on curated issues following full coverage, with a forecast date stated when the backfill ends (roughly 30 days at the observed inflow, not a delivery promise). Compare with the fixed baseline and report uncertainty."

> 5. The rollout ticket names Sophie for the policy read; Mnemosyne has [accepted E2, sibling parity and measurement ownership](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21005#discussioncomment-19631322) under the existing contributor program. Record each author’s explicit first-use response to the scoped offer; preserve declines and objections. Record the rollout start at the first E1 backfill edit or first scoped assistance offer, whichever occurs earlier. Review 14 calendar days after that start, including zero assisted PRs or a still-blocked execution gate; do not wait indefinitely for a first uptake. Record each sub-path’s enable/use dates so unequal exposure is visible. E1’s effect is reviewed at the 75-opening read, not day 14; the assistance safety/incident decisions remain at day 14 and immediately per incident. Record completion, repeat participation, maintainer effort, rebase requests, defects, consent objections, initially checked invitation boxes, E1 coverage and missed release notices separately. Reuse the program’s return measure; do not invent a contributor score or claim causality.

From criterion 6, the sentence that binds this read: "E1/E2 need observed coverage/replay/assignment receipts before claims of benefit."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The rollout start is recorded: the first backfill edit or the first scoped assistance offer, whichever is earlier, and each sub-path's enable and first-use date separately.
- [ ] Day 14 after that start, also with zero assisted pull requests or a still-blocked gate: a comment on #20892 reports coverage of the claim line over all open curated issues, and the count of unclaimed openings with its interval. It gives no verdict on E1's effect. It also reports how many openings GitHub could not assign because the author had not commented on the issue (30 of 87 in the 30 days to Nov 15; review 5912188398 on neomjs/neo#21040), so that the question whether such an author is told how to be shown as assignee is decided on a count.
- [ ] The same comment reports separately: completion, repeat participation, maintainer effort, rebase requests, defects, consent objections, initially checked invitation boxes and missed release notices. Sophie is named for the policy read of these.
- [ ] Every effort or wait time the read reports is attributed by the actionable handback that actually happened, the prerequisites that were available and the next owner. Unfinished and unknown intervals are shown as such, and who spoke last allocates no time. From the Discussion's evidence section: "A new read must classify the actionable handback, prerequisites, next owner and unfinished/unknown intervals." The actor-hour split of the first census is not reused.
- [ ] At 75 openings on curated issues after full coverage: a comment on #20892 compares the unclaimed rate with the frozen baseline under the same definition and reports the interval. A rate still near one third is reported as no demonstrated reduction; an inconclusive comparison is reported as inconclusive.
- [ ] If E1c's trigger fired (an issue missed the line because no maintainer filed or labelled it), the read says so and names the issue.
- [ ] No claim of benefit is made before coverage, replay and assignment receipts of E1 and E2 are linked.

## Out of Scope

The assistance trial's per-incident stops (the policy stream decides those at once). A contributor score. A causal claim.
